author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook entry for working at Redwood Inference. It summarizes our values and day-to-day expectations, the role and career ladder framework, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the core internal tools new and existing employees should know. Use this as your first-stop reference; teams should publish role-specific supplements where needed.

1) Working at Redwood — mission, values, and expectations

Summary
- Mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.
- Culture: engineering-first, product-minded, metrics-driven, and customer-focused.
- Day-to-day expectations: collaborate asynchronously, prioritize reliability and maintainability, and document decisions in Confluence or ADRs.

Key working norms
- Asynchronous collaboration: default to async updates in Confluence or PR descriptions. Schedule synchronous time for planning, incident response, and design reviews.
- Code ownership: adopt team-level ownership; small, frequent PRs are preferred.
- Decision records: use ADRs (architecture-and-standards/decision-records) for non-trivial design choices.
- Respectful feedback: follow our feedback rubric (constructive, evidence-based, timed) during reviews and 1:1s.

Work modalities and time off
- Flexible remote-first work model with optional in-office days by team.
- Core hours: 11:00–16:00 local time for team overlap; individual schedules tracked via your manager.
- PTO: unlimited paid time off with recommended minimum 15 business days off per year; use Concur for extended leaves.

2) Roles and career ladders

Principles
- Career ladders reflect scope of impact, complexity of problems solved, leadership (individual contributor vs manager), and measurable outcomes.
- Leveling is role-specific (Engineering, Product, Design, SRE, Sales) but follows a common rubric: Execution, Ownership, Complexity, Impact, Mentorship.

Engineering ladder (summary)
- IC-1 (Associate Engineer): writes well-scoped code, follows established patterns, requires regular mentorship.
- IC-2 (Engineer): independently delivers features, owns small services or components, starts mentoring interns.
- IC-3 (Senior Engineer): drives design for cross-team components, shapes architecture and reliability improvements.
- IC-4 (Staff Engineer): influences multiple teams, leads large projects, and sets technical direction.
- IC-5 (Principal/Distinguished): long-range technical vision, represents Redwood in external forums, leads major platform initiatives.

Manager ladder (summary)
- Mgr-1 (Engineering Manager): manages a single team (6–10 engineers), handles performance coaching, and delivers team roadmap.
- Mgr-2 (Senior Manager): manages managers or multiple teams, coordinates across functions.
- Director and above: organization-level strategy and cross-functional alignment.

Career development practices
- Quarterly calibration: level reviews are synchronized with performance calibration windows.
- Career conversations: managers hold at least two documented career conversations per year.
- Promotions: promotion packet includes written self-assessment, manager assessment, examples of impact, and peer feedback. See the promotion checklist in People Ops templates.

Ownership and role definitions
- Every role has a short role description, primary responsibilities, and OKRs. Teams must publish these in confluence/team-wiki or product-docs/requirements.

3) Benefits and perks (summary)

Health and financial benefits
- Medical, dental, and vision coverage: comprehensive plans with US and EU options. Coverage details in benefits portal.
- Retirement: 401(k) with company match (US); local-equivalent pension plans where applicable.
- Equity: standard RSU/grant program for full-time employees; details in offer letters and Equity FAQ.

Time off and family leave
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver, 8 weeks secondary caregiver (US baseline; local policies may vary).
- Caregiver leave: short-term caregiver leave available through HR.
- Volunteer time off: 2 paid days per year for approved volunteer work.

Compensation and perks
- Competitive salary bands with yearly compensation review cycles.
- Learning & development stipend: prorated L&D budget per head (see People Ops reimbursement process).
- Home office stipend: one-time setup stipend for remote hires and ongoing monthly co-working allowance for eligible roles.
- Wellness stipend and employee assistance program (EAP).

Other perks
- Regular offsites, team social budgets, and speaker series.
- Conference and training allowance (pre-approval required).
- Snack and local commuting stipends where offices exist.

How to access benefits
- Submit enrollment through the HR portal (Workday/Greenhouse links listed in people-ops/team-wiki). Contact benefits@redwoodinfra.com for exceptions.

4) Hiring and onboarding overview

Hiring process (standardized pipeline)
- Step 0: Recruiter screen — 30 min: culture fit and role alignment.
- Step 1: Technical screen or take-home exercise — role-dependent (30–90 min).
- Step 2: Onsite loop (virtual/in-person) — 3–5 interviews: coding/design, product sense, system design, culture and team fit.
- Step 3: Hiring committee review and compensation approval.
- Step 4: Offer and background checks.
- Typical time-to-offer: 2–4 weeks for most engineering roles; accelerated tracks exist for mission-critical hires.

Interview guidance
- Interviewers use structured rubrics and provide written feedback within 48 hours.
- Diversity-friendly interviewing: follow inclusive hiring guidelines; avoid biased questions; focus on demonstrated skills.

Onboarding framework (first 90 days)
- Pre-start (before day 1): IT onboarding ticket created by People Ops, access to Slack, Okta, email, and Confluence; hardware shipped.
- Week 0–1: orientation sessions (People Ops, Security, Platform orientation), manager 1:1, team intro, and OKR alignment.
- Month 1: small scoped onboarding project, documentation deep-dive, and mentor pairing.
- Month 2: increased ownership, first performance check-in, and cross-team introductions.
- Month 3: promotion to full ownership of initial scope; 90-day feedback review with manager and People Ops.

Onboarding checklist (required items)
1. Confirm hardware and VPN/KMS access.
2. Complete security and compliance training (within first 7 days).
3. Set up GitHub, CI permissions, and repo access.
4. Complete payroll and benefits enrollment.
5. Attend product and platform orientation.
6. Deliver first-week sync note to manager and team.

New hire mentor program
- Every new hire is assigned a buddy and a technical mentor for first 90 days. Mentors are expected to hold weekly check-ins for first 6 weeks and quarterly check-ins thereafter.

5) Internal tools guide (core systems and quick-start links)

Required tools (access provided during pre-start)
- Slack — company communication and team channels. Channels are prefixed by team name; general announcements in #company-all.
- Confluence — canonical documentation. Use the company-handbook and team spaces for policies and runbooks.
- Okta — single-sign-on for applications.
- GitHub Enterprise — primary code host. Follow repo CONTRIBUTING.md and branch protection rules.
- CI/CD: Buildkite for production builds; quickstart for PR pipelines in eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build.
- Issue tracker: Linear for product & design; Jira is used by Platform and SRE for operational tracking (see eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts).
- Monitoring & paging: Datadog for metrics, Sentry for error reporting, and PagerDuty for on-call rotations.
- Cloud console: GCP (hosted backend) and AWS for certain infra teams. Ask Cloud Infra for access.
- Internal analytics: Metabase for product metrics and billing dashboards.

On-call and incident tools
- PagerDuty for incident notification. Follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process runbooks for escalation.
- Incident writeups: use the postmortem template in confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems and tag the incident with the appropriate SLO and severity.

Security and compliance tools
- 1Password for shared secrets and team vaults.
- KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments are controlled by the Security team; request via security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions.
- Audit logging: access logs retained per policy; see security-and-compliance/audit-logging for retention windows.

Tooling best-practices
- Principle of least privilege: request access only for services you need; managers must approve elevated privileges.
- Document runbooks: if you touch production systems, publish an owner-runbook in eng-sre/runbooks.
- Cost awareness: reference the finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting cost center tags when provisioning cloud resources.

6) Ownership, escalation, and support contacts

People Ops
- For benefits, payroll, and onboarding issues — people-ops@redwoodinfra.com

IT & Security
- For hardware and access requests — it-support@redwoodinfra.com
- Security incidents and vulnerability reporting — security@redwoodinfra.com or use the anonymous reporting form in security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.

Facilities and office support
- Office reservations and expenses — workplace@redwoodinfra.com

7) Frequently asked questions (high-level)

Q: How do I start a promotion?
A: Talk with your manager to draft a promotion packet. See People Ops promotion checklist and schedule a calibration meeting.

Q: Who approves remote work allowances?
A: Your manager approves recurring co-working allowances; People Ops approves one-time home office stipends.

Q: Where are the performance goals stored?
A: Team-level quarterly OKRs should be stored in confluence/<team-space>/roadmap-and-themes and linked to individual goals in your 1:1 notes.

Appendix: Links and templates
- New hire 90-day plan template: confluence/company-handbook/onboarding-90-day-template
- Promotion packet template: confluence/company-handbook/promotion-packet-template
- Security training checklist: confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/training-checklist

If you have updates or spot inaccuracies in this page, file a change request in Confluence and tag people-ops and your manager. For urgent corrections to benefits or legal language, contact finance-and-legal.
